title: The geometry of absolute separability and other convex matrix properties from spectrum
authors: Jennifer Ahiable, Naga Bhavya Teja Kothakonda, Andreas Winter
abstract: We investigate the geometric structure of the set of spectra of bipartite absolute separable states ($\mathrm{ASEP}_{m,n}$) and absolute positive partial transpose states ($\mathrm{APPT}_{m,n}$), i.e., bipartite quantum states that remain separable or PPT respectively, under all global unitary transformations. First, we establish general geometric properties of absolute convex sets of matrices, their spectra and extreme points. Regarding absolute separability, we present a permutation-symmetric reformulation of the absolute PPT criterion and use it to demonstrate that $\mathrm{APPT}_{m,n}$ is a spectrahedron for all $m\leq n$: in particular, all its faces are exposed. In contrast, while $\mathrm{ASEP}_{2,n}$ is also a spectrahedron, we prove that in general $\mathrm{ASEP}_{m,n}$ is a semialgebraic set for all $m\leq n$. Furthermore, we provide a complete characterization of the faces and extreme points of $\mathrm{APPT}_{m,n}$ and demonstrate that the dimension of a face is determined by the rank of a certain matrix, with maximal proper faces having dimension $(mn-m-1)$.   In the quantitative setting, we provide a rigorous lower bound on the maximal attainable purity of $\mathrm{APPT}_{m,n}$ via an inscribed polytope $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$ and conjecture that the maximal purity of $\mathrm{APPT}_{m,n}$ (along with its spectra) coincides with the polytope for arbitrary dimensions except when $m=n=2$. Additionally, we also provide a rigorous upper bound on the minimal von Neumann entropy of $\mathrm{APPT}_{m,n}$ and demonstrate numerically that the minimum entropy eventually coincides with the polytope $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$ as the local system dimension $n$ increases. Finally, we show that the relative spectral volume of $\mathrm{APPT}_{m,n}$ decays exponentially in $n$ by a constant multiplicative factor of the relative volume of the inscribed polytope $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the complex geometry of sets defining separable or positive partial transpose bipartite quantum states. It proves that the set of absolute PPT states forms a spectrahedron, while the absolutely separable states are more general semialgebraic sets. The work provides deep structural insights into these boundaries using advanced tools from convex and algebraic geometry.
main_problem: The paper investigates the geometric structure of the spectra for bipartite quantum states that satisfy absolute separability ($	ext{ASEP}_{m,n}$) or are absolutely positive partial transpose ($	ext{APPT}_{m,n}$). It aims to characterize these sets using tools from convex geometry.
main_result: It proves that $	ext{APPT}_{m,n}$ is a spectrahedron with exposed faces, while $	ext{ASEP}_{m,n}$ is generally only semialgebraic. Furthermore, it provides structural characterizations of the boundaries and extreme points for both sets.
method: The methodology combines convex geometry (studying absolute convex sets and their spectra) with algebraic techniques involving polynomial determinants derived from permutation group actions on matrix representations.
model_or_system: The focus is on bipartite quantum states $ho \in M_m \otimes M_n$, specifically those satisfying the criteria of absolute separability or absolute PPT, which are constrained by global unitary transformations.
key_observables: Maximal attainable purity, minimal von Neumann entropy, relative spectral volume, and the geometric structure (spectrahedra/semialgebraic sets) of $	ext{APPT}_{m,n}$ and $	ext{ASEP}_{m,n}$.
important_parameters: The dimensions $m$ and $n$ of the bipartite system; the indices related to permutations in $S_{m,n}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing general geometric properties of absolute convex sets and utilizing advanced results concerning linear determinant preservers on symmetric matrices.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes general geometric properties for absolute convex matrix sets. It then applies these tools to characterize $	ext{APPT}_{m,n}$ as a spectrahedron and $	ext{ASEP}_{m,n}$ as semialgebraic. Finally, it uses permutation group theory and determinant polynomials to precisely map out the boundary structure of $	ext{APPT}_{m,n}$.
why_interesting: The rigorous geometric characterization of entanglement witnesses (like PPT/separability criteria) is fundamental for understanding quantum correlations and resource theories in quantum information.
